title: Error Design Practices & Smells
body:
# Error Design Practices & Smells

## Meaningful errors beat strings

Library/domain code defines its own error enum:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
enum ConfigError {
    #[error("config file unreadable: {0}")]
    Io(#[from] std::io::Error),
    #[error("invalid JSON at line {line}")]
    Syntax { line: usize },
    #[error("missing field `{0}`")]
    Missing(&'static str),
}
```

`thiserror` derives Display + From conversions so `?` composes across layers.
Application entry points may flatten with `anyhow`; **libraries return typed
errors** so callers can match.

## Smell: unwrap() in library code

```rust
// BAD: one malformed line takes down the process
let port: u16 = raw.parse().unwrap();
```

**Why:** you convert recoverable data into an abort.
**Refactor:** propagate — `raw.parse::<u16>()?` or map_err into your enum.
`expect("reason")` is acceptable for *invariants* you can prove at a call site,
with a message explaining why it cannot fail.

## Smell: panic-driven control flow

Using `panic!` / array indexing to signal expected conditions makes callers
unable to recover. If a condition is *expected*, model it in the type:
Result/Option first.

## Smell: overly generic error handling

A single `Error(String)` variant forces string-matching upstream. Enumerate
real failure modes; let the compiler enforce handling each one.
